_comment: Expected ParsedHackathon[] produced by LumaParser.parse() when the mocked fetch call returns luma-response-example.json for every slug ('tech', 'ai', 'crypto'), with the test clock frozen at 2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z (see NOW in luma-fixtures.test.ts). Dates are stored as ISO strings here because JSON has no Date type -- the consuming test parses them back into Date objects (`new Date(...)`) before comparing against LumaParser's actual Date output. The third event in the raw fixture ('Hackathon Winners Celebration Party') is intentionally absent: LumaParser's isHackathon() exclusion patterns filter out post-event celebration posts, so it never reaches the output. Because the same raw fixture is served for all three Luma slugs, LumaParser's own deduplication (by name + date_start) collapses the 3x-duplicated entries down to one of each. `topics` is pinned to `[]` for both events even though the raw descriptions clearly mention AI/blockchain/web3 keywords: lib/topic-extractor.ts's TopicExtractor constructor escapes the '|' alternation separator it just joined its keyword list with (its char-class escape regex includes '|'), so every compiled topic pattern is currently unmatchable and extractTopics() always returns []. This is a known, tracked production bug (issue #8, 'Fix topic-extractor regex bug'), not a mistake in this fixture -- once #8 is fixed, this fixture's `topics` arrays should be updated to ['AI'] and ['Crypto', 'Web3'] respectively.
